<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **39** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c1a645e2f0b7bdb124c10ae969ff631ff55bb5e9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `b71abe3075aee4546eef907fbcb0bebbd4dda0c7`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #32929 (body and every comment, ruling record 6840525219 included), PR #32982 (body, file list, net diff at the head), the check-runs on the head. Face: declaration (`Clause-②: no`; the six paths decide no schema or rules face). The code the diff calls (`resolvePackageScopedHolders`, `describePackageScopedHolder`, `typeLabel`) and the callers of `packageScopedRefusalMessage` were read at the head to judge the diff, not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. Answers unchanged: holds.** The only code hunk is the `outside-closure` case of `packageScopedRefusalMessage` in `packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts`: one template literal grows a sentence, plus a comment. `resolvePackageScopedHolders` (which callers are refused, which item resolves, the reason, `candidates`) is untouched, and so is every door's status and code mapping. The other four reasons' sentences are byte-identical. No test or code in the tree matches the sentence's tail: every reader test asserts `toContain` on the head (`held outside the declared dependency closure of package ...`), and the picklist boot-audit regex matches only the head as well.

**2. Arm selection: there is none, and that is correct.** The new sentence is a static conditional ("If that package already depends on P, the dependency would be a cycle: move what reads it into that package, or move the TYPE into P (ADR-0150 D3)."). It picks nothing from data, so there is no dependency check to get wrong. The message builder has no closure function in reach (it takes only the refusal), so a data-driven arm would have needed new plumbing; the static form names both fixes on every refusal, which is what ruling 6840525219 (a) asks. The unqualified "already depends" is right for direct and transitive dependency alike: P declaring the holder closes a cycle either way, and the kernel refuses both at boot (measured on the card: `Circular dependency detected`).

**3. Both fixes named, generic over every type: holds.** The sentence names the ruling's three moves (declare a dependency; when the holder already depends on the caller, move the reading item to the holder or the read item to the caller), in that order, and promises nothing beyond them. The type word comes from `typeLabel`, which renders every member of `PACKAGE_SCOPED_TYPES` plus `function` in plain words (`email template`, `permission set`, `sharing rule`, ...), so the sentence reads correctly for datasets, picklists, flows, functions, webhooks, permission sets and the rest. Both moves are sound in the cycle case: the holder already depends on P, so an item moved into the holder still reaches P's items, and an item moved into P is reached by everything that already depended on P.

**4. Tests: adequate for a static sentence.** `packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.test.ts` adds two cases under `[#32929]`: the whole sentence pinned with `toBe` for a dataset (reason, candidates and both fixes in one assertion), and the type-label interpolation for `email_template`. With no runtime arm there is no second branch to pin; the one sentence carries the plain fix and the cycle fix together, and a revert to the old text turns the `toBe` red. Not pinned: the sentence with an environment holder or with two holders (see nits N1, N2).

**5. The three corrected changesets: truthful about the exposure, one claim beyond the ruling.** In each note the original sentence is kept verbatim and the correction is appended, so no other meaning changes: `32072` scopes its zero to "read in this repository" and adds HotCRM's tile; `32310` adds HotCRM under "Who moves"; `32311` adds the cycle case to "The fix for those" and names HotCRM. The HotCRM facts match the card's measurement (app package dashboard, module-held `product_metrics`, 409 `outside-closure` once the console sends the caller package, drew on 18.3.0, the reverse dependency refused at boot), and each ends with "Other first-party apps outside this repository: not measured." Two gaps, graded below: S1 (all three notes state how HotCRM will fix it, which the ruling leaves open) and S2 (a fourth pending note makes the same zero claim and is not corrected).

**6. Design concerns (folded here; the declaration face carries no ④).** The new sentence inherits two weaknesses of the old one, neither a regression: it says "that package" when the only candidate is the environment (a documented `outside-closure` path), and when several packages hold the name (N1, N2). And one composed refusal outside the diff now contradicts itself (N3).

Findings:

- **S1 (should-fix).** `.changeset/32072-dataset-resolve-by-package.md`, `.changeset/32310-dataset-caller-package.md` and `.changeset/32311-dataset-caller-package-ui.md` each say "HotCRM moves that dashboard into the module that holds the dataset (#32929)." Ruling record 6840525219 lists exactly this under "Not ruled here": HotCRM may instead move the dataset into the app package, and the HotCRM lane picks. A pending release note should not state an unchosen downstream fix as fact. Reword in all three, e.g. "HotCRM moves either the dashboard into the module or the dataset into the app package (#32929)."
- **S2 (should-fix).** `.changeset/32077-dataset-query-package.md` (pending for 18.4.0, unchanged by this PR) still says "No first-party package references a dataset across packages." HotCRM's CRM Overview does exactly that. Ruling 6840360115 named `32077` for the same correction; record 6840525219's list names three other notes, so the floor's letter is met, but its intent ("correct the 18.4.0 changesets that state first-party exposure is zero") covers this sentence too. Correct it in this PR (a fourth DELIBERATE CORRECTION) or say on the PR why it is left.
- **N1 (nit, pre-existing).** `resolvePackageScopedHolders` step 3 adds `{ kind: 'environment' }` to the `outside-closure` candidates, and `32311` names environment-authored datasets as one of the two cases that stay refused. For an environment-only holder both sentences address "the package that holds it" / "that package", which does not exist; "move the TYPE into P" is the only fix that applies. The first sentence already had this flaw; the new one repeats it.
- **N2 (nit, pre-existing).** With two or more package holders outside the closure the sentence still speaks of "that package" in the singular, and declaring every holder would turn the refusal into `ambiguous-in-closure`.
- **N3 (nit, outside the diff, follow-up).** `packages/cli/src/utils/stored-package-references.ts` (the bind refusal for `outside-closure`) appends "... declare the dependency instead. Nothing written." to `answer.message`, so the composed sentence now offers the cycle moves and then names only the dependency. The PR body lists the picklist hint and the publish probe as sibling sentences for the follow-up; this one is not on that list.
- **N4 (nit).** `32310`'s "The remedy." paragraph still names only the dependency (and the qualifier); the cycle moves appear in `32311` and the runtime sentence but not there.
- **N5 (nit).** The new changeset's "Measured on HotCRM's shape ... after, the same sentence followed by ..." reports the after-sentence as measured; on the card only the before-sentence was read at the door, and the after-sentence is pinned by the unit test.

No must-fix.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/core` (`.changeset/32929-outside-closure-cycle-fix-sentence.md`): correct. Only a refusal's wording changes; no status, code, candidate list, resolution or spec key moves, and the message is not a contract any consumer in the tree parses past its head. `Clause-②: no` is right (no direction arm: nothing widens or narrows), and so is `Metadata-protocol: none` (no metadata-protocol baseline moves). `Check Changeset`'s LEVEL AXIS step agrees: clause-② `no`, metadata-protocol `none`, no entry at `minor` or above, no `major`. The three corrected notes keep their own levels and frontmatter; only body text moved.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`Check Changeset`: red, as designed for this class.** `check-empty-changeset` refuses the three edited notes (`32072`, `32310`, `32311`) as present on the merge base and changed by this PR. The gate never accepts a DELIBERATE CORRECTION: its own text says it stays red, that it is not a required context, and that the dispatching seat confirms the correction by its own record. The PR body declares the correction, names each note and quotes the corrected sentences, which is the shape the gate asks for. This record finds the corrections truthful about the exposure, with S1 and S2 as should-fix; confirming the correction is the dispatching seat's act, not this record's.
- **Other check-runs at read time:** 22 success, 11 skipped, 29 in progress (Build Core, Test Core 1-8 of 8, Test UI 1-16 of 16, the Type Check jobs, four Lint jobs, the E2E UI jobs). No other failure. This verdict does not stand in for the in-progress runs.
- **Scope held to floor (a).** The authoring refusal (`indexResolvableDatasets` in `packages/lint/src/validate-widget-bindings.ts`), the CLI picklist hint and the publish probe's `widget_not_probed` sentence are out of this PR and carried to the 18.4.1 follow-up the ruling allows. Until then `os validate` / `os build` still accept the tile the runtime refuses; the ruling accepts that for 18.4.0. Floor (b), HotCRM's own release, is in another repository and not judged here.
- **Unmeasured, carried on the card:** whether 18.4.0's runtime refuses the three HotCRM app actions that start module flows (`campaign_contact_member_enroll`, `campaign_lead_member_enroll`, `quote_generation`).
